title: An adjunction whose left adjoint preserves finite products lifts to abelian group and commutative ring objects
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be categories with finite products (final objects $*$), and $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ left adjoint to $R:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$; assume $L$ preserves finite products ($L(*)$ final and $L(X\times Y)\to LX\times LY$, induced by the projections, an isomorphism); $R$ preserves all limits, in particular finite products. For an abelian group object $(X,+,0,i)$ of $\mathcal A$ let $L(X)$ carry $L(+)\circ\lambda^{-1}:LX\times LX\to LX$, $L(0)\circ\lambda_*^{-1}:*\to LX$, $L(i)$, with $\lambda$, $\lambda_*$ the comparison isomorphisms; likewise $R$, and likewise for commutative ring objects (also $\cdot$ and $1$). Then: (1) these are abelian group (resp. commutative ring) objects, and $L$, $R$ so extended are functors $L^{\mathrm{gr}}$, $R^{\mathrm{gr}}$ on abelian group objects (resp. $L^{\mathrm{rg}}$, $R^{\mathrm{rg}}$ on commutative ring objects), commuting with the forgetful functors to $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B$; (2) for an abelian group (ring) object $X$ of $\mathcal A$ and $Y$ of $\mathcal B$, a morphism $\alpha:LX\to Y$ commutes with the structure maps if and only if its adjoint $R(\alpha)\circ\eta_X:X\to RY$ does; hence $L^{\mathrm{gr}}\dashv R^{\mathrm{gr}}$ (resp. $L^{\mathrm{rg}}\dashv R^{\mathrm{rg}}$), with adjunction bijection the restriction of that of $L\dashv R$, and unit and counit those of $L\dashv R$ (which are morphisms of group, resp. ring, objects).

source.place: Proposition 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi), proof of (2) ('adjointness follows from adjointness of the set based functors', details left to the reader) and the paragraph on rings as sextuples; the discussion before it ('the axioms are going to be preserved because f^{-1} is a functor which commutes with finite limits')
